title: Rai Bhoi's Death and the Minister's Counsel to Babur

blocks.text: The page closes the Rai Bhoi thread by showing how badly wisdom is repaid under corrupt rule. Rai Bhoi was slain without offense, and there was great outcry because the ruler had destroyed his own well-wisher instead of listening to him.

From that lament the narrative pivots into Babur's next decision. Though Babur was made ready to advance on Hindustan, his advisers insist that conquest cannot be undertaken blindly in a land guarded by saints and holy men.

The minister's counsel focuses above all on Guru Nanak. Babur is told to seek Guru Nanak's permission before marching further, because temporal force alone will not be enough if the spiritual order of India stands against him.
